Maria L.: quick sync — following up on the allocator-stitch RFC we merged last week. I ran a strawman integration with tenant-level kv-caching and hit a couple of awkward cases around small-page coalescing vs pinned-paths. TL;DR: we need a lightweight way to 'stitch' adjacent allocations into a single eviction unit without breaking the existing pin/unpin semantics.

Ken P.: can you sketch the bad case? :thinking:

Maria L.: sure. imagine frequent tiny activations that are pinned briefly (micro-batches). if the allocator aggressively coalesces them into a compact slab, we lose the ability to evict unrelated pages without stalling the pinned ones. result: spikes in latency when GC touches those slabs.

Ashok S.: sounds like the classic tradeoff: compaction wins for fragmentation but loses for eviction granularity. what did the strawman do?

Maria L.: added a 1-byte marker in the allocation header — a "stitch token" — that signals “group these pages for compaction but treat as a soft group for eviction”. eviction logic checks token and if present tries to evict the whole group unless any page is currently pinned in a high-priority path.

Paige R.: hmm — how does this interact with the guest KV cache layer? we already have a per-tenant hotset pin path that bypasses eviction when hits are > X. we don't want the stitch token to promote accidental pin-holds.

Maria L.: good question. proposal: guest-kv sets a separate bit (guest-hot). eviction policy treats stitch+guest-hot as guest-owned group: do not evict unless fallback policy kicks in (e.g., tenant throttle or global OOM). otherwise, stitch groups are fair-evictable.

Ken P.: implementation nit: can we avoid extra memory in hot allocations? adding bytes to every header for tiny allocations is expensive. maybe encode stitch groups in a side-table keyed by arena id + offset?

Maria L.: I tried side-table but the lookups added measurable CPU overhead in microbenchmarks. tradeoff: header byte (fast check, cheaper CPU) vs side-table (save RAM but cost CPU). current numbers: header + token increases resident footprint by ~0.6% on our test VMs, while side-table increases CPU median p99 by ~8ms per allocation under microbatch load.

Ashok S.: 0.6% memory vs 8ms is an easy call for latency-sensitive inference. lean towards header token. also can we TTL tokens for long-lived slabs so they decay into normal slabs after quiet periods?

Maria L.: yes — propose token with epoch counter: when stitch group is cold for N epochs we clear token (background compaction worker). typical value N=5 (configurable).

Paige R.: for guest-kv, I'd prefer an explicit API: guest layer can opt-in when it creates the cache region. that makes semantics clear and avoids accidental promotion. also add a telemetry label so we can measure how often stitch groups prevent eviction.

Ken P.: +1 to opt-in API and telemetry. also, add a fast-path in the eviction loop: if a stitch token is set and none of the pages in the group are pinned, evict whole group in one batched IO/ops. reduces churn.

Maria L.: noted — action items: (1) change: header token + epoch TTL (2) guest-kv opt-in API + telemetry tag (3) eviction fast-path for whole-group evict. will draft a follow-up RFC with microbench numbers and proto patch.

infra-bot: CI: build/linux-x86_64 #14251 passed — 3 tests flaky flagged. https://ci.internal/14251

Ashok S.: can you include the microbench harness and the side-table numbers? curious about tail effects across tenants.

Maria L.: yes — I'll attach both graphs and the harness in the RFC. planning to land experiment branch in staging tomorrow. ping me @Paige R. for guest-kv API review.

Paige R.: I'll review tomorrow after the release window. thanks for the clear plan. :thumbsup:

Ken P.: thanks — looks practical.

Maria L.: thanks all — closing this thread, will post the RFC link when ready.
